Young Men’s Christian Association of Montreal 


For release Tuesday, November 5, 1968. 
YMCA LANGUAGE COURSES SEEN KEYS TO CITIZENSHIP 


International Branch of the Montreal YMCA will this week honor 
some 250 adults for having taken steps to span one of the major 
obstacles to first-class citizenship in Canada. 


Their achievement--learning Inglish or French--will be cited 
this Wednesday and Thursday, at 8:00 p.m., at language classes 
graduation exercises in the branch. 


Most of those ta be honored are recent immigrants to Canada and 
family breadwinners. Their language certificates represent hours of 
classwork and studying, put in after days of hard labor or stints on 
the night shift. 


For many, the job of learning was further complicated by gaps 
in their educational background. Few of them had even completed 
elementary school in their native land. 


Motivated by the desire to earn a better living, they were 
eager to learn as much, and as quickly, as possible. While studying, 
they also acquired a better understanding of their adopted homeland, 
its value systems, and their rights and responsibilities. 


Encouraged by their progress to date, many representatives of 
this group have already enrolled for further training in International 
YMCA's language program. Courses starting November 18 are expected 
to attract some 400 persons. 


International YMCA now offers seven levels of classes in English 
and four in French, Teaching methods and the curriculum have been 
updated, and a comprehensive system of oral testing developed to 
ensure students are being taught at the appropriate level.
